issues: Per-keystroke latency (~104 ms median on 3696 rows) is essentially unchanged after React.memo on SheetCell. Root cause is elsewhere: (a) useSheet.applyPatch does rowsRef.current.map() over all 3696 rows for the immutable update, (b) useSheet.filtered useMemo iterates all 3696 rows on every rows change, (c) the parent creates a fresh `sheet` object each render ({...sheetBase, onContextMenu}) which is stable-enough for the current memo comparator but still triggers reconciliation of the ~600 SheetCell wrappers. Recommend: split rows into an immutable structure (immer/mutable index update) OR debounce filtered recompute, OR memoize by row (row-level memo component around each <tr>) so only the changed row re-renders.

action_items: OPTIONAL: The React.memo on SheetCell landed but didn't move per-keystroke latency (still ~100 ms). If further perf matters, memoize at the <tr> level and/or replace the O(N) `filtered` useMemo with an incremental filter, or wrap `applyPatch` to only recreate the changed row (Object.assign into a shallow-cloned array without full .map). This is a follow-up perf tuning, not a blocker.
critical_code_review_comments: useSheet.applyPatch (L101-108) uses rows.map() to build the next array on every keystroke - O(N) copy of 3696 rows dominates the 100ms budget. Consider `next = rows.slice(); next[idx] = { ...next[idx], ...patch };` (already O(N) for slice but half the work of .map with predicate).

useSheet.filtered useMemo (L113-119) re-runs on every rows identity change (every keystroke). For 3696 rows without active filters it still does .map(...).filter(...). Cache the trivial no-filter case and reuse the previous array.

OrderSheet.jsx L58 creates a new `sheet` object per render (spread + onContextMenu). Because SheetCell.memo comparator ignores `sheet` identity this is currently OK, but any future prop added to the destructure of `sheet` will silently defeat memoization - add an ESLint rule or a useMemo wrapper.

useSheet.newRow inserts a trailing blank row on every applyPatch when the last row was written (L104). Combined with 3696 rows this keeps growing the rows array; verify a stress test with 5000+ writes still trims correctly (line 439 pad handles it on refresh, but not between refreshes).
server.py list_order_rows .to_list(5000) still caps at 5000 while DB has 3696 rows - 1.4x safety. Recommend cursor-based pagination or bump to 20000.

rca of the issue: iter11 burst crash: fixed by (a) rAF-throttling recompute in useWindowRows (drops chained scroll->setRange->render loops to one per frame), (b) early-return in scrollToRow when target row is already inside the visible window, (c) setAnchor skipping setSel when the single-cell anchor didn't move. All three fixes verified: 200 ArrowDown + 200 ArrowUp bursts produce zero console errors, zero overlay, and the focused cell / grid scroll continue to track correctly.
